name: The Furnace Below Meridian
description:
The debut album from Kofi Strand-Yaroslav, released in 2223 at age nineteen, The Furnace Below Meridian arrived without press, without label support, and without a name attached — the artist withheld identity for the first three months, distributing through encrypted mesh networks under the tag 'nobody.shelf.m88.' When Strand-Yaroslav was eventually identified, the revelation that the album had been recorded over eighteen months in a Tier 1 basement using salvaged equipment and a cracked AI composition assistant became inseparable from the music itself. The album blends Shelf noise, Yoruba talking drum patterns, Central Asian throat singing techniques, and fractured electronic production in a way that sounds simultaneously ancient and broken-new.

Standout tracks include 'Furnace Address,' the album's eight-minute opener, which begins with a field recording of the Shelf's industrial district at 3 a.m. before a talking drum pattern emerges from the noise and pulls the track upright; 'Meridian Youth,' a three-minute piece of startling directness — Strand-Yaroslav's voice alone over a single sustained note, listing the names of people from their block who died in a building collapse in 2221, the note dropping one quarter-tone every thirty seconds; and 'Below,' the closing track, a twenty-minute drone that listeners have described as 'the sound of a city that doesn't know you exist, and the specific feeling of deciding that's all right.' Vantablack Media's A&R division made contact within a week of the artist's identification. Strand-Yaroslav has not responded.
creator: Kofi Strand-Yaroslav
genre: Shelf noise / polyrhythmic electronic / drone folk
audience: Shelf youth, underground music communities across all tiers, music critics, Tier 3 cultural commentators, anyone who finds it
cultural_impact: The Furnace Below Meridian is the most-discussed debut album in GLMZ in a decade. It arrived at a moment when the conversation about Shelf art and Shelf voices had become loud enough to reach Tier 3 media, and it refused every frame that conversation tried to put on it — it was not a poverty narrative, not a protest record, not an appeal for sympathy. It was something harder to categorize: a young artist from the most forgotten tier of the city making something of rigorous, formal beauty out of the materials at hand. The Tier 3 music press called it the album of 2223. Underground Shelf networks said the Tier 3 press had missed the point entirely. Both were probably right.
story_hooks: Kofi Strand-Yaroslav has gone silent — no mesh activity, no new music, no response to anyone. Their neighbors say they haven't been seen in two weeks. Vantablack Media denies involvement, but the timing of their A&R contact and the disappearance is uncomfortably close.

A Tier 3 music publication wants to run the definitive profile of Strand-Yaroslav and hires the party to locate the artist — who may not want to be found, may be in danger, or may be deliberately testing whether anyone will come looking.

The cracked AI composition assistant Strand-Yaroslav used on the album has been traced — it contains fragments of several other unreleased works, and the corporation that originally owned the AI wants them back, regardless of what that means for the music.
